name: Gluteal Tendinopathy
summary: Load-related gluteus medius/minimus tendon pain, usually presenting as lateral hip pain and often overlapping with GTPS.

looksLike: Pain with single-leg stance, stairs or lying on side
redFlags: Acute trauma with inability to bear weight
Systemic illness, fever or unexplained weight loss
firstSteps: Reduce compressive positions and excessive adduction

tests.name: Resisted Hip Abduction
tests.purpose: Load gluteal tendons and reproduce familiar lateral hip symptoms.
tests.positive: Familiar lateral hip pain or pain-limited weakness.

stages.label: Protection, Education & Symptom-Guided Loading
stages.goal: Address safety, settle excessive irritability and maintain useful movement.
do: Reduce compressive positions and excessive adduction
dose: Avoid prolonged hip-crossed sitting if it provokes symptoms
moveOn: Daily function is stable or improving.
No new red flags or progressive neurological deficit.
Exercise response returns to baseline by the following day.

stages.label: Mobility, Strength & Capacity
stages.goal: Restore the specific strength, mobility and control required by the condition.
when: Daily function is stable or improving.
No new red flags or progressive neurological deficit.
Exercise response returns to baseline by the following day.
do: Add pelvic control and single-leg functional work
moveOn: Target movement and resistance are tolerated with good quality.
Functional capacity is improving without sustained symptom flare.
Progression is based on objective performance and patient goals.

stages.label: Functional Restoration & Return to Activity
stages.goal: Rebuild real-world, occupational or sporting capacity.
when: Target movement and resistance are tolerated with good quality.
Functional capacity is improving without sustained symptom flare.
Progression is based on objective performance and patient goals.
do: Progress heavier, faster and multiplanar loading
Maintain strength two or more times weekly
dose: Running progression with planned recovery days
moveOn: Full task exposure is completed progressively.
No clinically meaningful deterioration during the following 24 hours.

returnCriteria: Strength and running tolerance restored progressively

mechanism: Repeated tensile loading combined with compression in hip adduction
Rapid increase in running, stairs or single-leg loading
classification: Reactive or persistent tendon-related presentation; clinical staging is not reliably determined by imaging alone
investigations: Clinical diagnosis is common; imaging if suspected tear, stress fracture or persistent uncertain presentation.
Do not use tendon imaging changes alone to explain symptoms.
manual: Manual therapy only for relevant coexisting impairments; avoid painful direct compression.
Education and progressive loading have stronger rationale than passive tissue techniques.
modalities: Positioning and temporary load modification are useful.
Injection decisions belong to medical shared decision-making; repeated injections may not support long-term tendon capacity.
mistakes: Using pain-free palpation as the only discharge measure
pearls: The LEAP trial supports education plus exercise for gluteal tendinopathy.
Manage tendon compression as well as tensile load.

tests.name: Resisted Hip Abduction
tests.purpose: Load gluteal tendons and reproduce familiar lateral hip symptoms.
tests.positive: Familiar lateral hip pain or pain-limited weakness.
tests.patientPosition: Side-lying with tested hip neutral or slight extension; stabilise pelvis and resist abduction.
tests.therapistPosition: Position yourself to observe and stabilise the relevant segment without forcing the movement.
tests.handPlacement: Use comfortable, controlled contact appropriate to the test; avoid painful compression or excessive force.
procedure: Explain the test and obtain consent.
Screen contraindications and compare sides when appropriate.
Perform the movement slowly and apply only the required resistance or stress.
Record familiar symptom reproduction, range, strength and side-to-side difference.
tests.interpretation: Interpret with symptom location, single-leg loading and differential screening.
tests.clinicalNote: A special test modifies clinical probability; it does not confirm a diagnosis in isolation.
